comparator.name: Media and Culture
comparator.route: Dutch-language track — Performing Arts and Creative Technologies
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized Dutch title Media en Cultuur selects the OER’s Dutch-language track rather than the separately documented English track. The official 2026-2027 OER fixes a 180-EC curriculum: a 120-EC major and 60-EC profiling space. The major contains two four-course basic packages (60 EC), one four-course depth package (30 EC), a compulsory philosophy course (7.5 EC), one restricted-choice course (7.5 EC), a research seminar (7.5 EC), and the thesis (7.5 EC). The target does not name one of the four depth packages, so Performing Arts and Creative Technologies is selected by official order before considering UCR fit. Kunst, cultuur en maatschappij is selected by the same official-order rule from the two restricted choices. The profiling space remains open.
components: Agenda Setting in Arts and Culture

routeSelection.route: Dutch-language track — Performing Arts and Creative Technologies
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the Dutch programme title Media en Cultuur, so the Dutch-language track is selected independently of UCR fit. Within that track the target does not name one of four equally formal 30-EC depth packages; the current OER lists Performing Arts and Creative Technologies first, so official order resolves that nested choice. Kunst, cultuur en maatschappij is likewise the first restricted-choice course. The 60-EC profiling space remains open.

alternatives.label: Media, Film, Performance & Cultural Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates film and media, literature, visual culture, history, sociology, philosophy and research across a broad cultural-analysis pathway.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines film and media analysis with storytelling, visual and performance culture, media history, heritage, identity, society, philosophy and qualitative humanities research.
progression: Introductions to visual culture, literature, film, history and sociology precede advanced film-and-text analysis, media and race, museums, social theory, creative communication and independent historical research. All formal prerequisites and verified semester offerings are respected; eight level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Participatory Media, Production & Sustainable Culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum connects audiovisual analysis and communication with audiences, social research, identity, organisations, platforms and cross-media practice.
alternatives.concept: A participatory-culture pathway connecting audiovisual media and creative communication with audiences, production, identity, social research, environmental communication, organisations and sustainable cultural change.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, ten courses replace literary survey, broad art-history, heritage and historical-research coverage with rhetoric, audience methods, environmental and climate communication, organisational psychology, leadership, market research and contemporary social analysis. The 75-EC change creates a participatory, production- and sustainability-centred pathway.
progression: Introductory media, rhetoric, sociology and research methods precede documentary and environmental media, audience research, social theory, persuasive and creative communication, organisational leadership and market research. Every course is in a verified offering and formal prerequisites are met.

alternatives.label: Critical AI, Platforms & Digital Society
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule mirrors the neutrally selected formal package through media theory, digital platforms, visual and data methods, algorithms, society, representation and advanced communication research.
alternatives.concept: A critical digital-culture pathway combining media and communication with data science, computer vision, databases and machine learning, situated through sociology, political philosophy, ethics and research.
progression: Introductory communication, film/media, data science and brain-and-behaviour work precede advanced persuasion, platforms, machine learning, psycholinguistics and research. Qualitative and data methods support critical study of algorithms and digital society; every course is offered in its assigned semester.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, thirteen courses replace literary, art-historical and heritage study with applied rhetoric, data science, computer vision, databases, machine learning, platform media, cognition and advanced research. Eleven courses differ from the participatory pathway, clearly distinguishing critical AI and digital infrastructure from audience, production and sustainability study.

blocks: Both introduce film and audiovisual-media history, form and critical analysis.
Both trace changing media technologies and forms historically; UCR uses media-archaeological methods.
Both introduce analytical foundations for digital media and data-driven culture; UCR emphasises computational data literacy.
Both examine television and its transformation within platform and social-media cultures.
Both compare modes of storytelling and representation across periods and media; UCR focuses on myth and literature.
Both critically examine what art communicates and how institutions shape cultural value; UCR focuses on modern art and museums.
Both compare meaning across media and examine intermedial relations; UCR focuses on adaptation between film and text.
Both develop research, selection and interpretation for presenting cultural material; UCR is art-historical rather than a dedicated curating course.
Both treat creative, embodied and mediated communication as cultural practice; UCR offers a broader creative communication laboratory.
Both use creative humanities and communication to intervene in urgent social questions; UCR centres the climate crisis.
Both analyse agenda setting, framing, persuasion and influence in public culture.
Both introduce qualitative research design and methods for analysing representation, production, audiences and cultural meaning.
Both develop philosophical reflection on knowledge, value and responsibility in cultural research; UCR concentrates on ethics.
Both examine institutions, cultural value and the relation between culture and society; UCR approaches these questions through contemporary social theory.
Both culminate in advanced research design and independent inquiry, though UCR uses psychology rather than media-and-culture methods.
The selected UCR courses do not directly cover this dedicated Utrecht component or curricular function; it remains a visible programme difference.
The Utrecht programme preserves 60 EC of profiling space; the fixed 24-course UCR alternative has no directly corresponding open component.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme-wide media-analysis, cultural meaning, performance, identity, history and technology interests. All four official depth directions were assessed. Participatory Cultures and Critical AI generate the strongest feasible and most distinct additional UCR pathways; their schedules differ from the closest match by ten and thirteen courses and from one another by eleven. Media Heritage and Performing Arts are also evidence-backed directions, but the three-programme maximum has been reached.

notes.text: Utrecht requires dedicated introductions to film, television, new media, theatre and dance; a complete four-course depth package; media-and-culture research preparation; and a bachelor thesis. UCR can build strong combinations in film and media, communication, literature, art history, sociology, philosophy, data science, sustainability and empirical research, but lacks dedicated television and performance sequences, professional media-production and curating infrastructure, and a compulsory bachelor thesis; the standardised Optional independent research element remains optional.
